items.content_html:
Summary

This is an alternative proposal for #30437.

Basically, the idea this:

  • All values (marked in code in the lists below) are direct sub-features of the CSS property like done everywhere else in the BCD CSS property tree. The support data for these values is whenever the value was first introduced, no matter which context, so their pure first existence.
  • If consumers want to know when the property and all of their values are usable in a specific context, then they can consult the special context_* behavioral sub-features to get that information
  • If a value for a given context is not supported at the same time as the context and has existed before for a different context, the value gets also added to the context as a sub-feature. (this is a special case, and you can see it in effect in the second example for stretch).

This is exercised on two properties: css.properties.align-content and css.properties.align-self.

  • css.properties.align-content:

    • context_block
    • context_flex
    • context_grid
    • context_multicol
    • baseline
    • center
    • end (new from split)
    • first baseline
    • flex-end (new)
    • flex-start (new)
    • last baseline
    • normal
    • safe (new from split)
    • space-around (new)
    • space-between (new)
    • space-evenly
    • start (new from split)
    • stretch
    • unsafe (new from split)

  • css.properties.align-self:

    • context_flex
      • stretch (different to the original stretch as well as different to context_flex)
    • context_grid
    • context_position_absolute
    • anchor-center
    • auto
    • baseline
    • end (new from split)
    • first baseline
    • last baseline
    • normal
    • safe (new from split)
    • start (new from split)
    • stretch (the original stretch implementation)
    • unsafe (new from split)

Test results and supporting details

I updated the ordering lint to put the contexts at the top, much like we do for workers or for secure_context_required.

Related issues

#30437
items.title: Restructure CSS properties which contain contexts

items.content_html:
Summary

Add some keys representing a new behavior in module loading, where HTTP errors aren't cached, so developers can now retry loading a module that failed to fetch.

Test results and supporting details

This is a spec change and (I think) one that is impossible to feature detect, so this makes a good fit for a behavioral subfeature.

I didn't test this, but it's well attested through bugs:

  • Chromium enabled it in 156 (tracking bug).
  • WebKit added it with r319474. The Safari TP release notes don't mention it by name, but it was included in the range of changes given by the 252 release notes. When I tried the WPT test on Safari 27, it failed.
  • Firefox bug 2055211 shows this shipping in 154.

Setting the spec URL was difficult. There's nothing in the spec that screams that this should work the way it does, but you can see whatwg/html#10327 and tell me if you've got a better idea here.

Lastly, I added three keys since I believe these are the three entry points for this behavior. See #30304 for further discussion.

Related issues

  • Fixes #30304
  • Prompted by web-platform-dx/web-features#4335
  • Spec change: whatwg/html#10327

Add compatibility data for the soft and off values of the HTML <textarea wrap> attribute.

The parent wrap support data is broadened where needed so it covers both values.

  • Chrome (16), Edge (12), Firefox (4), Opera (≤12.1), and Safari (6) reuse the existing wrap versions for both values.
  • Internet Explorer uses ≤4 for wrap, off, and soft, based on Microsoft's historical IHTMLTextAreaElement.wrap documentation.

items.content_html:
Chrome and FF only support writing one ClipboardItem - tested using (async (i = (t) => new ClipboardItem({ "text/plain": t })) => navigator.clipboard.write([i("a"), i("b")]).then(() => "resolved", (e) => ${e.name}: ${e.message}))().
Safari allows writing as many as you like.

The spec says that you may write more than one item if the OS supports it but that if not only the first item may be writen.

But what happens on Chrome/FF is a NotAllowedError exception - the spec says that additional items should be ignored.

(async (i = (t) => new ClipboardItem({ "text/plain": t })) => navigator.clipboard.write([i("a"), i("b")]).then(() => "resolved", (e) => `${e.name}: ${e.message}`))()

Promise { <state>: "fulfilled", <value>: "NotAllowedError: Clipboard write is only supported with one ClipboardItem at the moment" }

I added this as a note, but wondering if it should be a subfeature or this is OK? (or something else)

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#45430
items.title: Clipboard.write() - only supports writing one ClipboardItem on Chrome/FF

items.content_html:
Towards #30410

According to the Collector, support goes a long way back. I assume these values have been introduced with the initial Flexbox implementation which would make sense given BCD originally didn't have initial CSS values as sub features. They were mass-added by Vinyl in 2025.

Also, these Flexbox sub-features probably weren't added back then because the structure is not simple: There is nesting going on here where values sit below flex_context and grid_context. You can also see this in the compat table on MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/align-content#browser_compatibility

I think we want the following structure, but it would be good to confirm it before I proceed with other CSS properties. Is it correct to put all these values under flex_context?

  • css.properties.align-content:
    • block_context
    • flex_context
      • baseline
      • center
      • end (new from split)
      • first baseline
      • flex-end (new)
      • flex-start (new)
      • last baseline
      • safe (new from split)
      • space-around (new)
      • space-between (new)
      • space-evenly
      • start (new from split)
      • stretch
      • unsafe (new from split)
    • grid_context
    • multicol_context
    • normal

Alternatively, I guess, we could flatten this all out, leading to a few moves plus adding the missing values. That would mean less work for me on the Collector side, as I still have to teach the Collector that these values can be found in subtrees (flex_context in this case, grid_context in other cases).

What do we think?
items.title: Add missing CSS flexbox property values

items.content_html:
Summary

As per #30358 (comment), This PR aims to make CSS data more consistent in cases where a feature (property or type) started its life off not animatable, but was made animatable later on.

In such cases, I am using the following keys:

  • is_animatable when the data point describes when the feature was made @keyframe animatable, or @keyframe animatable and transitionable.
  • is_transitionable when the data point describes when the feature was made transitionable.

And the following description structure:

  • "@keyframe animatable" when the data point describes when the feature was made @keyframe animatable.
  • "Transitionable" when the data point describes when the feature was made transitionable.
  • "@keyframe animatable and transitionable" when the data point describes when the feature was made @keyframe animatable and transitionable.

The description also has an optional suffix: "when x", where x is a particular condition under which the feature is animatable and/or transitionable. For example — "@keyframe animatable and transitionable when setting inset properties"

Notes:

  • text-combine-upright started off animatable in Fx, but that was a mistake, and it was corrected per spec later on. I don't think this is worth adding a separate data point for, so I've just left that one as a note.
  • I've not added a guideline for this yet, as I'm not sure where to do that. I am hoping the above will for the basis of that.

Test results and supporting details

Related issues
items.title: Make CSS is animatable data consistent

The new data covers both API paths where the parameter can be provided:

  • RTCRtpSender.setParameters() via parameters.encodings
  • RTCPeerConnection.addTransceiver() via init.sendEncodings

Test results and supporting details

  • BCD linting passed with no errors.
  • The test suite passed: 338 tests passed, 0 failed.
  • git diff --check passed.
  • Chrome support is recorded from version 111 based on the WebRTC SVC implementation.
  • Firefox and Safari are recorded as unsupported for this specific encoding parameter.

Supporting specification:
https://w3c.github.io/webrtc-svc/#dom-rtcrtpencodingparameters-scalabilitymode
